## Overview

You have been writing R code in [Quarto {{< fa external-link >}}](https://quarto.org/){target="_blank"} documents
since week 12.
This week, we will take a closer look at the three components of Quarto documents:
the **YAML header**, **code chunks** and **text**.
We will use more options to customize your documents and to
display/hide code and figures, and see what happens when you render a document.
We will also see how to record the R and package versions you used.

## Lectures & Learning goals

Some of the things you will learn this week:

#### [Quarto and reproducible R workflows](./w14a_quarto.qmd)

-   What happens when Quarto renders a document
-   More about **YAML** syntax and useful options in the YAML header
-   **Chunk options**, including for figures, and how to set them for a whole document
-   How to include R output in your Markdown text
-   How to record the versions of R and R packages that you used
-   How to render a document to Markdown that displays well on GitHub

- [Additional Quarto material](/bonus/quarto.qmd):
  chunk labels, Positron's visual editor and inline chunk output,
  how to cache slow code chunks,
  and how to turn an R script into a Quarto document
- [R package environments with renv](/bonus/renv.qmd):
  how to give each project its own package library,
  and record and restore package versions
